IncompleteLineageRecord.description: A model whose column lineage is known to be incomplete (#2377).

gaps.description: The constructs in it that Rocky does not trace, such as `natural_join` or `set_operation`. `None` when they were never computed (unknown).

data_type.description: Inferred column type, rendered as a Rocky type string (e.g. `STRING`, `INT64`, `DECIMAL(10,2)`, `TIMESTAMP`). Omitted when the type could not be inferred — typically a `SELECT *` against an upstream whose schema isn't cached, or a model that did not pass typecheck.

LineageConsumerRecord.description: One downstream consumer in a `rocky lineage` view.

description.description: What it is for, when declared.

direct.description: `true` when the consumer reads the focal model itself; `false` when it reads only models downstream of it.

url.description: Where to find it, when declared.

transform.description: Transform kind: "direct", "cast", "expression", etc. Stringified from `rocky_sql::lineage::TransformKind` to avoid pulling schemars into rocky-sql.

LineageGap.description:
A construct whose lineage Rocky does not record, so a model that uses it has known-incomplete lineage (#2377).

Impact analysis (`rocky lineage --downstream`, the blast radius) can then under-report: an edge the construct implies is missing. The list is what the extractor knows it skips. It is not a proof that everything else is traced.

oneOf.description: A `NATURAL` join. Its key columns are known only to the warehouse catalog, so no `join_key` edge is recorded.
`GROUP BY ALL`. Its group keys are not resolved, so no `group_by` edge is recorded.
A `UNION`, `INTERSECT` or `EXCEPT`. Value edges come from the first branch only; the other branches' columns are not mapped.
A filter, join, group, window or limit key inside a `WITH` body. Only the top-level query's row selection is recorded.
A filter, join, group, window or limit key inside a derived table (`FROM (SELECT …)`).
A subquery expression (`IN (SELECT …)`, `EXISTS`, a scalar subquery). Its columns and predicates, and any correlated reference, record no edge.
A window named after another named window. Its keys are not resolved.
A relation the extractor does not read: `PIVOT`, `UNNEST`, a table function, `APPLY`, `ARRAY JOIN`, `LATERAL VIEW`, `CONNECT BY`, or a `VALUES` body.
A column whose table cannot be determined statically (an unqualified column in a multi-table query). Its edge is dropped.
A projection item whose output column lineage could not name (`SELECT (x)`, `SELECT 1`).
A `SELECT *` over a relation whose columns Rocky does not know, so the expanded columns have no edges.

LineageNodeDef.description:
Per-node metadata for the lineage graph.

One entry per distinct model referenced by `LineageOutput.edges` (plus the focal model). Carries cluster keys consumers can use to group nodes without having to parse the qualified node name. Either optional field may be absent — `target_schema` is `None` for nodes that aren't project models, and `source_id` is `None` for nodes that are project models (i.e. the two fields are mutually exclusive in practice).

model.description: Qualified node identifier as it appears in `edges[].source.model` and `edges[].target.model`. Stable across the rest of the payload.

source_id.description: Source identifier for nodes that represent an external source (i.e. a referenced table outside the project model set). The value mirrors how the SQL referenced the source so consumers can key on it directly. Omitted for project models.

target_schema.description: Resolved target schema for project models, from the model's declared target config. Omitted for external sources and any node Rocky couldn't resolve to a project model.

description:
JSON output for `rocky lineage <model>` (model lineage shape).

When invoked with `--column <col>` (or `model.column` syntax), the dispatch returns `ColumnLineageOutput` instead — the two shapes share version/command/model headers but otherwise differ enough to keep separate.

consumers.description: Downstream consumers (dashboards, notebooks, ML jobs, applications declared in `consumers/`) that read the focal model, directly or through the models downstream of it. Sorted by name. These are not models, so they are not part of `downstream`. Omitted when none.

incomplete_lineage.description:
Models in this view (the focal model and every model upstream and downstream of it) whose lineage is known to be incomplete, sorted by name (#2377). Impact through them may be under-reported. `[]` means none.

Always written. A payload with no such field comes from an older build: read it as unknown, never as complete.

nodes.description: Per-node metadata for every model referenced by this lineage view (the focal model plus each endpoint of `edges`). Lets consumers (e.g. the VS Code subgraph drill-in) cluster nodes by their resolved target schema or source identity instead of parsing the qualified node name. Empty when no nodes were resolved; older JSON payloads cached locally may omit the field entirely.
